```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source("../setup.R")
docs_setup(legend = "bottom")
```

Position adjustments separate marks that share coordinates and arrange groups within each data cell. This article uses repeated observations and grouped columns to show jitter, dodging and stacking, including labels that follow the adjusted positions. Installation and three-dimensional mappings are covered in [Get started](ggplot3d.html).

1. **Map** the groups that share a position with `aes(group = )`.

2. **Adjust** the geometry with a position such as `position_dodge_3d()` or `position_stack_3d()`.

3. **Label** the adjusted marks by giving `geom_text_3d()` the same position.

## Example

```{r packages, message=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggplot3d)
```

### Separating repeated observations

The table below has six observations at each of four x/y positions. Their heights are identical within each position. [position_jitter_3d()](../reference/position_jitter_3d.html) adds uniform noise within the specified distance on each axis; setting the height to zero preserves the measured heights. A fixed seed makes the displayed positions reproducible.

```{r jitter, fig.alt="Six observations at each of four positions spread horizontally while retaining their original heights."}
observations <- expand.grid(x = 1:2, y = 1:2, replicate = 1:6)
observations$z <- observations$x + observations$y
ggplot(observations, aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  geom_point_3d(colour = "#2E6F9E", size = 2,
    position = position_jitter_3d(width = 0.15, depth = 0.15,
                                   height = 0, seed = 14)) +
  coord_3d()
```

Jitter changes the displayed positions, so the spread in this figure is introduced by the adjustment. Use explicit widths when the spacing between observed values would give an unsuitable default. [position_nudge_3d()](../reference/position_nudge_3d.html) applies a fixed offset, for example to move labels above their points.

```{r nudge, fig.alt="Four points with their height labels shifted upward by 0.3 units."}
centres <- unique(observations[c("x", "y", "z")])
ggplot(centres, aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  geom_point_3d(size = 3, colour = "#2E6F9E") +
  geom_text_3d(aes(label = z), size = 5,
    position = position_nudge_3d(z = 0.3)) + coord_3d()
```

### Comparing groups within cells

Each x/y cell in the next table contains values for groups A and B. [position_dodge_3d()](../reference/position_dodge_3d.html) places those groups beside each other along x or y. An explicit shared width keeps the column and text layers aligned.

```{r dodge, fig.alt="Two labelled columns at each x/y cell, with group A and group B separated along x."}
values <- expand.grid(x = 1:2, y = 1:2, part = c("A", "B"),
                       stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
values$z <- c(2, 3, 4, 2, 3, 2, 2, 4)
dodge <- position_dodge_3d(axis = "x", width = 0.8)
grouped <- ggplot(values, aes(x, y, z = z, group = part))
grouped +
  geom_col_3d(aes(fill = part), width = 0.7, depth = 0.55,
              position = dodge) +
  geom_text_3d(aes(label = part), position = dodge, vjust = -0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(name = NULL, values = c(A = "#2E6F9E", B = "#9E5E0F")) +
  coord_3d()
```

The default `preserve = "total"` divides each cell among its present groups. Choose `preserve = "single"` to retain the group width set by the fullest cell when some groups are absent. A label layer needs the same group mapping and cell membership as its columns.

### Showing totals and proportions

Stacking adds the group values along an axis. [position_stack_3d()](../reference/position_stack_3d.html) stacks positive and negative values separately from zero. The text layer uses the same ordering, with its anchor halfway through each interval.

```{r stack, fig.alt="Two labelled sections in each column, stacked to show each cell's total."}
grouped +
  geom_col_3d(aes(fill = part), position = position_stack_3d(),
              width = 0.6, depth = 0.6) +
  geom_text_3d(aes(label = part),
    position = position_stack_3d(vjust = 0.5)) +
  scale_fill_manual(name = NULL, values = c(A = "#2E6F9E", B = "#9E5E0F")) +
  coord_3d()
```

The fill adjustment divides each positive stack by its total. These data are all positive, so every column ends at one. For signed data, negative values are normalised separately and extend toward minus one.

```{r fill, fig.alt="Four columns reaching one, divided into the proportions contributed by groups A and B."}
grouped +
  geom_col_3d(aes(fill = part), position = position_fill_3d(),
              width = 0.6, depth = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(name = NULL, values = c(A = "#2E6F9E", B = "#9E5E0F")) +
  scale_z_continuous(name = "Proportion", breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
  coord_3d()
```

Stacking requires a shared zero baseline and a linear continuous scale along the stacking axis. Positions operate after scale transformation: a nudge of one on a base-ten log scale multiplies the original coordinate by ten. [Scaling heights and facet ranges](z-scale.html) explains transformations and limits.

## Projecting onto panes

To show a cloud's margins, use [position_project_3d()](../reference/position_project_3d.html). It projects the layer onto a chosen pane or a plane at a data value. [Combining 2D and 3D graphics](combining-2d-3d.html#projecting-points-onto-the-floor-and-walls) works through floor and wall projections, including two-dimensional marginal plots.

Position support depends on the geometry. The layer's help page lists supported adjustments; an unsupported combination reports an error. [Choosing layers for observations and grids](layers.html) includes examples of columns, bands and area walls that can be stacked.
